title: Add config change webhook + internal event stream for Optimization Config apply/promote/rollback
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Internal-only: emits Optimization Config lifecycle events (apply/promote/rollback) to an event stream and optionally delivers them to registered webhooks for Redwood tooling (e.g., incident-bot annotations, rollout dashboards). No customer-facing API exposure in this PR.
description: Motivation: We need a consistent, machine-consumable signal when Optimization Config versions change (apply/promote/rollback) so internal tooling can annotate dashboards, kick off automated checks, and attach context during incidents. Today, the source of truth is audit logs + DB state, which is not ideal for near-real-time integrations and requires each consumer to poll. This PR adds (1) an internal event stream publisher for Optimization Config lifecycle changes and (2) a webhook delivery mechanism for internal service integrations, with reliability guarantees and security guardrails. Scope: Events are emitted for Optimization Config actions: VALIDATE (success/failure), APPLY (staged start/pause/resume/complete/fail), PROMOTE, and ROLLBACK. Events use a stable schema (v1) modeled after CloudEvents-like envelope and include the minimum fields required for correlation (event_id, occurred_at, actor_type/actor_id, request_id, correlation_id, tenant_id, model, region, scope, config_version_id, previous_config_version_id (when applicable), rollout_id, and action/status). Implementation details: We introduce an outbox table (optimization_config_event_outbox) written in the same transaction as the config state transition to ensure we never publish an event that doesn’t correspond to persisted state (and we don’t miss events). A lightweight publisher worker drains the outbox, publishes to the internal event bus topic redwood.controlplane.optimization_config.v1, and (optionally) fans out to registered webhook subscriptions. Webhook subscriptions are internal-only for now: created/managed via internal endpoints guarded by service-to-service auth + RBAC permission optimization.config.webhook.manage, and secrets are stored via the existing secrets provider (no plaintext secrets in DB). Delivery: Webhook deliveries are signed with HMAC-SHA256 (X-Redwood-Signature, X-Redwood-Event-Id) and retried with exponential backoff + jitter. We enforce idempotency on the receiver side by documenting X-Redwood-Event-Id, and on the sender side by tracking delivery attempts keyed by (event_id, subscription_id) to avoid duplicates on worker restarts. Observability: Adds metrics for publish latency, delivery latency, attempts, and failure rate tagged with action/status, plus structured logs with event_id/request_id for easy joins with audit logs. Tests: Unit tests for schema validation and signature generation; integration tests for outbox draining + retry behavior using a fake HTTP server; and a regression test to ensure config apply/rollback continues to emit audit events (ENG-4826) even if webhook publishing is temporarily unavailable. Rollout plan: Ship behind feature flag optimization_config_change_events_enabled (default off). Enable in staging for incident-bot + dashboard annotations, then progressively enable in production for internal consumers. Related: Follow-on PR in incident-bot adds a shortcut command and uses these events for auto-linking rollback UI/runbook (see incident-bot PR-20081). Notes/Non-goals: This does not expose a customer-configurable webhook feature; it’s explicitly internal for now. We also do not implement guaranteed ordering across tenants/regions beyond per-rollout ordering best-effort; consumers must handle out-of-order events using occurred_at + state reconciliation.
commits: control-plane: add OptimizationConfigChangeEvent v1 schema + serializer
db: add optimization_config_event_outbox + webhook_subscriptions + delivery_attempts tables
workers: implement outbox drainer + bus publisher
webhooks: add signer (HMAC) + dispatcher with retries/backoff and per-subscription rate limits
authz: add RBAC permission optimization.config.webhook.manage + internal endpoints
metrics/logging: emit publish/delivery metrics and structured logs
tests: outbox transactionality + webhook retry + signature verification
docs: internal runbook notes for consuming events + example payloads
conversation: Jordan Lee (review): Outbox approach makes sense. Two asks: (1) Can we ensure the event is written in the same transaction as the config state transition? (2) Please document the consumer contract for out-of-order delivery and retries; consumers will treat these as at-least-once.

Benji Okafor (author): Yep on (1) — I refactored the state transition to accept a tx handle and write outbox rows before commit. Added integration coverage that fails if the outbox write is outside the transaction. On (2) I added a doc section + a note in the schema: delivery is at-least-once; consumers should de-dupe by event_id and reconcile by comparing config_version_id to current active pointer.

Kevin Osei (review): Security: please avoid storing any webhook secret material in DB. Also add a signature timestamp header or include occurred_at in the signed payload to reduce replay risk. Finally: ensure internal endpoints require service auth and are not reachable from customer-facing gateway.

Benji Okafor (author): Updated: DB now stores only secret_ref (Vault path) and a key_id. Dispatcher fetches secret at send-time with caching. For replay: signature is over canonical JSON payload including occurred_at plus subscription_id; added X-Redwood-Signature-Timestamp set to occurred_at. Internal endpoints moved under /internal/control-plane/* and require mTLS service identity + RBAC permission optimization.config.webhook.manage.

Allison Grant (review): Metrics tags look good. Can you add a gauge for outbox backlog size and a histogram for (occurred_at -> publish_time) to detect worker lag? Also please ensure config_version tag is present for delivery failures; we want to correlate with rollout health dashboard annotations.

Benji Okafor (author): Added outbox_backlog_total and publish_lag_seconds histogram. Delivery failure counter now tags tenant_id/model/region/config_version_id/action/status/subscription_id (with cardinality guardrails: subscription_id only in logs, not metrics). Config version is always included.

Jada Williams (review): For Console integration later, please confirm the event payload includes previous_config_version_id so we can generate a useful human diff link. Also: naming—can we use 'ROLLBACK' action with status 'COMPLETED' rather than a separate action 'ROLLED_BACK'?

Benji Okafor (author): Added previous_config_version_id for PROMOTE/ROLLBACK. Standardized actions to APPLY/PROMOTE/ROLLBACK/VALIDATE with statuses STARTED/PAUSED/RESUMED/COMPLETED/FAILED. Updated doc examples.

Connor O'Brien (review): Release coordination: feature-flag default off is good. Please add a migration note for backfill/no-op behavior on existing config history. Also ensure the worker won’t spam if the bus is down; we don’t want unbounded retries.

Benji Okafor (author): Added release note: no backfill for historic events; only new transitions emit. Worker retry is capped (max_attempts=12) and uses DLQ table optimization_config_event_outbox_dlq after exhaustion with an alert. Bus downtime won’t cause hot loops (sleep/backoff).
Jordan Lee (final): Approved. Thanks for tightening the transactionality and docs.
Kevin Osei (final): Approved with security changes in place.
